1 Scientific Literature.Title: Multi-Scale Characterization of Industrial Steel Slags Using XRF and SEM–EDS Phase Mapping
1 Scientific Literature.Authors: Okhunjon Sayfidinov, Susheng Tan, Bakhtiyor Mardonov, Makhliyo Sayfidinova, Baibhaw Kumar
1 Scientific Literature.Study_Objective: Characterize four steel slags from different production routes at an Uzbek plant via XRF and automated SEM-EDS phase mapping to link chemistry, phases and process.
1 Scientific Literature.Abstract_or_Key_Finding: Two groups: Mn-Si-O slag (S1, Mn 58.7 mass%, MnSiO/MnO phases) from Mn-alloyed steel, and Ca-rich slags (Ca 83-88 mass%) dominated by Ca-F-O (CaF >98% in S2, S3) from fluorite fluxing; S4 heterogeneous with Mn, Zn, Cu. Ca-rich slags proposed for acid drainage neutralization, cement additive after stabilization; Mn slag for Mn recovery.
1 Scientific Literature.Notes: No cementitious testing; SCM only mentioned as prospect.

9 Citations & Provenance.Original_Source_Text_or_Excerpt: Sample 1 showed a manganese-rich bulk composition, with Mn as the dominant element at 58.7 mass%, followed by Si at 15.2 mass%, Ca at 14.1 mass%, and Fe at 6.38 mass%
Sample 2 contained 88.2 mass% Ca, with much lower levels of Fe at 3.29 mass%, Al at 2.80 mass%, Si at 2.10 mass%, and Mn at 1.85 mass%
Sample 3 showed a very similar pattern, with 86.4 mass% Ca, 3.42 mass% Si, 2.83 mass% Fe, 2.78 mass% Mn, and 2.77 mass% Al
Sample 4 also remained Ca-rich at 83.0 mass%, but it contained relatively higher Fe at 5.37 mass% and Mn at 3.71 mass%, together with Al at 2.90 mass% and Si at 2.93 mass%
